record.paper_title: Some open problems of Ramsey minimal graphs.
record.original_question: Let F, G, and H be non-empty graphs, and write F → (G, H) to mean that every red-blue coloring of the edges of F contains either a red copy of G or a blue copy of H. A graph F is Ramsey (G, H)-minimal if F → (G, H) but, for every edge e of F, the graph F − e fails to satisfy F − e → (G, H). Let ℜ(G, H) denote the set of all Ramsey (G, H)-minimal graphs. For each integer n ≥ 4, classify all graphs in ℜ(2K2, K1,n), where 2K2 is the matching consisting of two disjoint edges and K1,n is the star with one center and n leaves.

evidence.quote: F, G, and H, say that F → (G, H) if whenever the edges of F are 2-colored, say with red and blue, there is either a red copy of G or a blue copy of H. A graph F is called Ramsey (G, H)-minimal if F → (G, H) but for any edge e ∈ E(F), we have (F - e) ↛ (G, H). The set of all Ramsey (G, H)-minimal graphs, the topic of this note, is denoted by ℜ(G, H).
Problem 2. For each n ≥ 4, characterize the graphs in ℜ(2K2, K1, n).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let F, G, and H be non-empty simple graphs. Write F → (G, H) to indicate that for every coloring of the edges of F with two colors (red and blue), there is either a red subgraph isomorphic to G or a blue subgraph isomorphic to H. A graph F is said to be Ramsey (G, H)-minimal if F → (G, H) and, for every edge e ∈ E(F), the graph F − e satisfies (F − e) ↛ (G, H). Denote by ℜ(G, H) the class of all Ramsey (G, H)-minimal graphs (up to isomorphism).

Let 2K₂ denote the graph consisting of two vertex-disjoint edges, and let K₁,ₙ denote the star with one center vertex adjacent to n leaves.

Problem: For each integer n ≥ 4, give a complete classification (characterization) of the graphs in ℜ(2K₂, K₁,ₙ).
artifact.status_search_result: Mengersen and Oeckermann gave a characterization of graphs belonging to ℜ(2K₂, K₁,ₙ) for n ≥ 3, and determined ℜ(2K₂, K₁,ₙ) explicitly for small n (e.g. ℜ(2K₂, K₁,₂) = {2K₁,₂, C₄, C₅}). Subsequent work has continued to refine and extend these results, but a fully explicit list for general n ≥ 4 in completely closed form is not uniformly stated as settled in the literature; the structural characterization exists but explicit complete enumeration is treated as an ongoing problem.

status_evidence.title: On Ramsey (mK2,H)-Minimal Graphs - Graphs and Combinatorics
status_evidence.snippet: Mengersen and Oeckermann presented a characterization of graphs belonging to R(2K2, K1,n) for n ≥ 3.
status_evidence.claim: A structural characterization of ℜ(2K₂, K₁,ₙ) for n ≥ 3 has been given by Mengersen and Oeckermann.

status_evidence.title: On Ramsey (2K2, Wn)-minimal graphs of smallest order
status_evidence.snippet: R(2K2, K1,2) = {2K1,2, C4, C5}; characterization of graphs belonging to R(2K2, K1,n) for n ≥ 3.
status_evidence.claim: Explicit determination for small n and characterization for n ≥ 3 are known.
